title: Geometric Contact Flows: Contactomorphisms for Dynamics and Control
authors: Andrea Testa; Søren Hauberg; Tamim Asfour; Leonel Rozo
independent_acceptance: focused scientific check completed; scientific adjudication pending
summary: Printed splitting map violates contact preservation; proposed action/geodesic derivation fails for the paper's own latent model; local energy exponent sign error.
limitations: No author-code execution or empirical reproduction.
Extended experimental and quantum claims not fully verified.

problems.title: Printed kinetic splitting map is not contact
problems.claim_location: Section 4 p5; Appendix B.2 p16 Eq (33c); B.3-B.4 p17
assumptions: d=1; canonical eta=ds-p dq consistent with Eq31
H=p^2/2, M=1,V=F=0; smooth allowed scalar functions
problems.check: Compute pullback of eta by (q+tau p,p,s+tau p^2). Coefficient of ds forces conformal multiplier 1, while dp residual is tau p.
problems.result: Not a contactomorphism; residual 0.2 at stated test point. Correct exact s increment is tau p^2/2.
problems.counterevidence: B.3 reports residual <1e-5 for implementation; unavailable code prevents resolving different implemented formula. Visually confirmed printed formula.
problems.impact: Core contact-preserving network construction invalid as printed, not proof of empirical performance error.

correction.scope: Constant kinetic substep only; not full variable-M scheme.

independent_check.original_and_assumptions: Read physical pp.5,16,17 and bounded architecture passage p.19; viewed Eq.33c. Eq.11 permits the smooth scalar constant M=1,V=F=0, so the first two substeps are identities. Standard eta=ds-p dq is consistent with Eq.31.
independent_check.independent_derivation: For Q=q+tau*p,P=p,S=s+tau*p^2, dS-P*dQ=(ds-p*dq)+tau*p*dp. The ds coefficient sets multiplier 1. At p=1,tau=1/5 the dp residual is 1/5, while Q=1/5 and S=1/5 from zero q,s. The exact Eq.31 flow has S=1/10 and zero residual. This was recomputed directly without relying on the initial diagnostic output.
independent_check.counterevidence_and_scope: The numerical residual claim in B.3 is about an unspecified implementation and does not change Eq.33c. A different contact convention would have to change Eq.31 as well. No code provenance or empirical score conclusion follows.
independent_check.severity_and_repair: Major retained: Section4 explicitly builds its contact architecture from this substep. The half-factor corrects only the constant kinetic case; no variable-M repair was certified.

problems.title: Unconstrained action and action-length identification fail for proposed latent model
problems.claim_location: Section3 p4 Eqs4-5; Appendix A.3 p15 Eqs29-30; Section5 p6 Eqs16-18
assumptions: Fixed-endpoint variation delta s=t(1-t); positive s for small perturbation
problems.check: First variation -integral_0^1 t(1-t)dt=-1/6. Actual ds/dt=-1 at t=0 but printed sqrt(H-HV)=+1.
problems.result: The contact solution is not stationary for Eq4; same s cannot be action and specified increasing length parameter.
problems.counterevidence: A constrained terminal-action principle or independent length parameter would be a different formulation; not justified by displayed Eq4 and appendix. Figure4 is illustrative not a proof.
problems.impact: Invalidates central derivation supporting geodesic/metric-reshaping interpretation. Does not refute usability of heuristic control objective or all possible geometric reformulations.

correction.scope: Needs new constrained variational formulation and equivalence proof.

independent_check.original_and_assumptions: Read p.4 Eqs.4-7 and p.15 Eqs.29-30, plus Section5 p.6 dependency. Eq.4 varies q,p,s with no displayed differential constraint; Eq.7b admits H=(q^2+p^2)/2+s.
independent_check.independent_derivation: Substituting q=p=0,s=exp(-t) into Eq.31 verifies all three equations. A compact-endpoint perturbation delta s=t(1-t) gives delta J=-[t^2/2-t^3/3]_0^1=-1/6. Both signs of sufficiently small epsilon preserve s>0, so the path is not stationary for the displayed unconstrained problem. At t=0 Eq.31 gives ds/dt=-1 while the stated square-root reparameterization gives +1.
independent_check.counterevidence_and_scope: Eq.29 calls the action implicit, which suggests a possible Herglotz-type intended reading, but does not supply the missing admissible-variation constraint or justify identifying this decreasing s with increasing length. Thus the finding concerns the written derivation, not impossibility of every constrained formulation.
independent_check.severity_and_repair: Major retained for the central Section3-to-Section5 geodesic justification. No false-theorem or failed-control-performance claim is added. A constrained variational formulation and separate equivalence proof remain necessary.

problems.title: Energy exponential has wrong sign
problems.claim_location: Section4 p4 Eq8 contrasted with Eq31 p16 and Eq40 p20
problems.check: Chain rule gives dH/dt=-H_s H; H_B at (0,0,1) has H(t)=exp(-t).
problems.result: Eq8 prints exp(+t) for this example.
problems.counterevidence: Eq40 already contains negative exponent; damping prose agrees with decay. No code evidence of wrong implementation.
problems.impact: Local energy-law error; not separately demonstrated to affect results.

independent_check.original_and_assumptions: Compared p.4 Eq.8 with autonomous Eq.31 on p.16 and the negative exponent in p.20 Eq.40.
independent_check.independent_derivation: The q and p cross terms cancel in grad(H) dot (H_p,-H_q-pH_s,pH_p-H), leaving -H_s*H. Hence H=H0 exp(-integral H_s), and Eq.7b along q=p=0 has H(1)=exp(-1), not exp(1).
independent_check.counterevidence_and_scope: Eq.40 and damping prose already use decay; the checked evidence cannot assign the error to training or inference.
independent_check.severity_and_repair: Minor retained for the local printed energy identity; sign replacement restores the autonomous identity only.

repair_verification: Exact constant kinetic substep and autonomous energy identity only; no full algorithm repair.
